title.en: Affordable Premium Web Design Switzerland: CHF 880 | Weissmann

metaDescription.en: Weissmann Starter Website: CHF 880 instead of CHF 2,490. Exactly what is included, what is not, who it suits, and when a larger package fits better.

h1.en: Affordable Premium Web Design in Switzerland: What CHF 880 Can Honestly Buy

answerFirst.en: Weissmann's Starter Website costs CHF 880 as a current special promotion, down from a regular price of CHF 2,490, as a one-time fixed fee. For that price you get up to five core pages of bespoke, mobile-optimized design, a contact or lead form, a technical SEO and GEO foundation, Google Analytics 4 and Search Console set up, basic structured data, performance optimization, security headers, Netlify deployment, one language, and two defined revision rounds. Copywriting, additional languages, and paid third-party tools are not included. This price applies to that specific approved scope, not to every website project — larger or more complex needs call for the Business or Complex tier instead.

heading.en: The Quote That Looked Like a Typo

paragraphs.en: Illustrative scenario: A consultant running a small advisory practice in Zug got two numbers in the same week. An agency quoted her CHF 11,400 for what she described, reasonably, as a clean five-page site. An hour later, browsing Weissmann's own pricing page, she saw CHF 880 for what read like a similar scope. Her first instinct was that one of the two numbers was wrong. That reaction is not unreasonable — in a market where a professional website routinely runs into five figures, a four-figure price with a higher figure crossed out next to it deserves exactly that scepticism.

This article exists to resolve that scepticism with specifics rather than reassurance. Two real prices sit on weissmann.ai/en/preise/ right now: CHF 2,490 as the regular price of the Starter Website, and CHF 880 as the current special promotion, a one-time fixed fee, not a subscription. What follows is the exact scope behind that number — every feature it includes, every feature it deliberately leaves out, who it actually suits, and the point at which a different Weissmann package becomes the honest recommendation instead.

heading.en: Two Real Prices, No Rounded-Off Percentage

paragraphs.en: It would be easy to turn CHF 2,490 versus CHF 880 into a headline built around a percentage, printed larger than either actual price. This article will not do that, and it is worth saying why. A rounded discount figure implies a baseline the reader has no easy way to verify and a temporary event with an unstated deadline. Two real prices, both visible on the live pricing page, are more useful to somebody actually deciding whether to spend money: CHF 2,490 regular, CHF 880 promotional, both fixed, both current as of this writing.

The more important clarification has nothing to do with arithmetic, though. CHF 880 is the price for one specific, clearly bounded package — the Starter Website — not a blanket rate that applies to every website Weissmann builds. Businesses that genuinely need more than this scope will pay more, and this article says exactly where that line sits, rather than letting anyone discover it midway through a project.

heading.en: What CHF 880 Actually Buys, Feature by Feature

paragraphs.en: The Starter Website is a fixed-price package with a defined, complete scope, not a stripped-down product that quietly needs extras before it works properly. Here is the full feature list, unchanged from the current pricing page:

bullets.en: Up to 5 core pages, responsive design, mobile-optimized
Contact or lead form
Technical SEO and GEO foundation
Google Analytics 4 and Search Console set up
Basic structured data, performance optimization, security headers
Netlify deployment, 1 language, 2 defined revision rounds

heading.en: What These Six Lines Actually Change

paragraphs.en: A few of those lines read like technical shorthand, and they are worth unpacking, because the difference they make is real even when it is invisible to a visitor. A technical SEO and GEO foundation means the site is structured so that both search engines and AI answer systems can actually parse and understand it from day one: correct page structure, a sitemap, sensible metadata, clean internal linking. It does not replace ongoing SEO work, and it does not guarantee a ranking — nobody could honestly promise that — but it means a new site does not start its working life at a structural disadvantage, which is the mistake a weekend-built template usually makes.

Security headers are the kind of invisible housekeeping a bargain builder tends to skip, precisely because nobody notices it is missing until a security scan or a search engine does. Google Analytics 4 and Search Console set up means a business owner can see, from week one, whether anyone is actually visiting the site and whether Google can find it, rather than discovering three months later that neither tool was ever connected.
And underneath all six lines: this is a fixed price. No hourly billing, no it depends at the final invoice, no surprise line item for something already listed above.
Equally important is what this package deliberately leaves out — not fine print discovered after payment, but stated here before any decision is made:

bullets.en: Copywriting: you supply the content for your up to five pages yourself, or copywriting is scoped and quoted separately in advance. The Starter package designs and builds the site; it does not write it for you.

Additional languages: one language is included. A bilingual site — commonly German/English or German/French for a Swiss business with international clients — needs either a larger package or a separately quoted language surcharge, because every additional language brings its own copy, its own metadata and its own SEO structure.
Paid third-party tools: subscriptions for booking systems, advanced form plugins, CRM connections or similar services are, if wanted, arranged and paid separately. They sit outside the fixed price.

heading.en: Three More Boundaries Easy to Miss on a First Read

paragraphs.en: Reading the feature list once tends to surface three further limits that are just as binding as the ones above, even though they are easy to skim past:

bullets.en: Page number six: the package is built for up to five core pages. If your business genuinely needs more structure — a second location, a blog, several distinct service pages — that is not an add-on line to the Starter price; it is a signal that the Business Website is the right category instead.

Revision round number three: two defined rounds are built in, for content and design refinement. A third, more fundamental change after the project is signed off remains possible, but as a separately scoped piece of work, not a silent extra on top of the fixed price.
E-commerce, booking or CRM integrations, member areas: these belong, in scope and in complexity, to the larger packages described further down, not to the Starter scope.

heading.en: Who the Starter Scope Is Actually Built For

paragraphs.en: This package is designed around a specific, genuinely common profile, not around any small business in general. It fits well when several of the following are true. You need a credible, professional presence with a clear structure — home, offer, about, work or references, contact — and five pages genuinely covers that. You are selling, largely, in one language to a largely single-language client base: a physiotherapy practice in Zurich, a trades business in Basel, an advisory boutique serving German-speaking clients that does not need to run the same site in three languages at once. You already have your copy written, or you are prepared to provide it yourself rather than commissioning an agency to write it. And what you actually need is a contact or lead form, not a payment-enabled shop or a booking engine.

Typical examples: a sole proprietor who has relied on a Google Business Profile until now and needs a real site to point clients to. A trades company that wants enquiries to arrive through a form instead of exclusively by phone. An advisory practice with a clear, contained offer that needs a credible presence quickly, without a six-month agency engagement.
A short self-check before you read further: if you can answer yes to all four of the following, the Starter scope is very likely the right one.

bullets.en: You can genuinely work within five pages.
You sell, in substance, in one language.
You have your own copy ready, or you are planning copywriting as a separate item.
You need a contact form, not a shop or a booking flow.

heading.en: When You Need a Larger Package Instead

paragraphs.en: There is a real point at which CHF 880 is simply the wrong question, not because the package is inferior, but because the actual requirement is a different one. The Business Website, at CHF 4,990, is built for growing companies that need a complete digital acquisition and conversion system, not a digital business card. It runs to roughly 10 to 20 pages per an agreed scope with premium custom design, a conversion-focused architecture and lead-generation system, advanced technical SEO and GEO optimization, multilingual readiness, a blog or knowledge section, advanced forms with booking or CRM connections where relevant, GA4 with conversion tracking and advanced structured data, and three revision rounds instead of two. If reading the exclusion list above produced more than one moment of actually, I do need that, this is the honest next category to look at.

For large multilingual architectures, custom applications, e-commerce, API and CRM integrations, member areas, dashboards, interactive tools or AI workflows, there is the Complex/Custom Website, from CHF 9,900, priced by scope rather than from a fixed catalogue. That is not an inflated barrier to entry; it is the realistic order of magnitude for work that goes well beyond a company website. An online shop with payment processing, shipping and product management, for instance, or a platform with a login area, belongs structurally in this category regardless of how small the business behind it happens to be.

heading.en: Premium Execution, Accessible Price — Not the Same as Cheap

paragraphs.en: An accessible promotional price and a cut-rate result are two different things, even though marketing language likes to blur the line between them. The distinction is already visible in the feature list above, minus the explanation for why it matters: bespoke design rather than a template, a technical SEO and GEO foundation rather than a site that merely happens to be online, Google Analytics 4 and Search Console properly configured rather than no measurement at all, performance optimization and security headers rather than a site that fails its first load test or security scan.

The positioning here is deliberately not as cheap as possible. It is premium performance and design without the traditional agency price tag, for a scope that is precisely defined rather than left to expand indefinitely. That is a genuine difference from do-it-yourself website builders, where the missing hours simply come out of your own calendar, and from conventional agencies, whose entry price is often several multiples of CHF 880 without the actual scope needed by a small business necessarily being any larger. The promotional price is a chance to get that standard of work at an unusually accessible entry point, not evidence that something was quietly cut to get there. Think of it less as a discount bin and more as a factory-direct price on engineering that was never redesigned to be worse.

heading.en: Where Fixed-Price Projects Actually Go Wrong

paragraphs.en: The most common friction on a project like this rarely has anything to do with the technology. It comes from expectations that shift midstream. Realistically, and without dramatizing it:

bullets.en: Scope quietly grows mid-project: five pages become seven in conversation, because a references page and a careers page both sound necessary once you start talking. Prevention: decide early which five pages genuinely matter, or move openly into the Business scope instead of stretching the Starter frame until it splits at the seams.

Copy is not ready at kickoff: because copywriting is not part of the package, timelines usually slip not because of the build itself but because the words are still being written while the project is already underway. Prevention: prepare your text as far as possible before the project starts, or budget copywriting explicitly as a separate item.

Ranking guarantees are quietly expected: a technical SEO and GEO foundation genuinely improves the starting conditions, but it does not guarantee a specific Google position or an AI citation, and no serious provider could honestly promise that. Prevention: treat the foundation as exactly that, a solid technical base, not a ranking commitment.

The need for a second language surfaces after signing: if it becomes clear mid-project that two languages are actually required, that is not grounds for an awkward surprise surcharge; it is a reason for an open conversation about moving into a larger scope.

heading.en: The One Decision That Actually Matters

paragraphs.en: Every consideration above collapses into a single, honest test: does your real requirement — page count, languages, a form rather than a shop, your own copy — fit inside the Starter scope described above? If it does, CHF 880 buys a bespoke, technically sound website project at an unusually accessible price. If your requirement runs past that boundary, the more honest move is to start at the Business or Complex category directly, rather than quietly shrinking a project to fit a lower number and renegotiating later.

The practical next step: check your own requirements against the feature list above, then look at the current figures and packages at weissmann.ai/en/preise/, where the same numbers, and the direct route to ordering, are always kept up to date.

a.en: We deliberately do not present it that way. What matters are two real, current prices: CHF 2,490 regular, CHF 880 as the current special promotion, both listed at weissmann.ai/en/preise/. A rounded percentage would make this read like a limited sales tactic; it is simply the current price for a precisely defined scope.

q.en: Does every website at Weissmann cost CHF 880?

a.en: No. CHF 880 applies only to the Starter Website scope described in this article: up to 5 pages, 1 language, 2 revision rounds. A project with more pages, more languages, a booking or CRM connection, or e-commerce sits in the Business category (CHF 4,990) or the Complex category (from CHF 9,900).

q.en: How long will the CHF 880 price stay available?

a.en: The current price is always shown, and kept accurate, at weissmann.ai/en/preise/. We are deliberately not stating an end date, a number of remaining slots, or a countdown here — not to dodge the question, but because we will not state something we cannot actually guarantee.

q.en: Is copywriting included in the price?

a.en: No. You provide the content for your up to five pages yourself, or copywriting is scoped and quoted separately in advance. The package covers design, technical build and structure, not writing your text.

q.en: How many languages are included in the Starter Website?

a.en: One. A bilingual or multilingual site — commonly German/English or German/French for a Swiss business with international clients — needs either a larger package or a separately calculated language surcharge, because each additional language brings its own copy, metadata and SEO structure.

q.en: What if I realize during the project that five pages are not enough?

a.en: Tell us before the scope quietly expands. Either we agree together on the five pages that matter most, or we move openly into the Business scope, at the Business price, not a retroactively inflated Starter price.

q.en: Is this template-based design, or something genuinely custom?

a.en: It is bespoke premium web design, not a page-builder theme with your logo dropped in. The promotional price is about the defined scope, not about reduced design quality.

q.en: What happens after the two included revision rounds?

a.en: The two rounds are meant for content and design refinement. A more fundamental change afterward — a new page concept, a different structure — remains possible as a separately scoped piece of work, not an automatic addition to the fixed price.
